findings.finding: The candidate directly rejects the misleading compiled-versus-interpreted binary and compares all three languages using the same translation-target and runtime-execution dimensions.

C++ statements are explicitly scoped to a typical Clang/GCC-style AOT toolchain and the answer separately acknowledges JIT/plugin/dynamic-code cases, so the common pipeline is not presented as a language mandate.

Java correctly separates javac class-file compilation from JVM execution, bounds HotSpot profiling/JIT behavior as an implementation strategy, and treats warm-up/deoptimization as possible runtime costs rather than universal language semantics.
Python claims are scoped to CPython, distinguish code objects/bytecode/.pyc caches from native AOT binaries, and explicitly warn that CPython bytecode is not a stable cross-implementation ISA.

Portability and performance claims remain conditional on target/toolchain/runtime/workload factors, the answer contains multiple topic-specific follow-ups, and no absolute C++/Java/Python speed ranking or fabricated personal project result is asserted.
